stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy receives filled and labelled vials from a central facility in another state that is not licensed by the Board. On arrival the pharmacist inspects each vial against the prescription and finds everything correct. May the pharmacy dispense them?

choices.text: Yes, because the pharmacist has personally checked each finished product.
Yes, because central fill is a recognised part of ordinary pharmacy practice.
No, unless the process was verified by a Massachusetts licensed pharmacist.
No, because a pharmacy may never dispense what it did not process itself.
No, unless the receiving pharmacy documents the inspection in the patient profile.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.04(11) bars a pharmacy from dispensing medication PROCESSED OUTSIDE ITS LICENSED PHARMACY PREMISES unless the PROCESS was VERIFIED BY A MASSACHUSETTS LICENSED PHARMACIST or was PERFORMED IN A PHARMACY LICENSED BY THE BOARD. The facility is not Board-licensed, so the second route is closed, and inspecting the finished product is not verification of the process.

choice_analysis.A: The requirement attaches to the process, not to the finished product.
choice_analysis.B: Recognition of the practice does not remove the regulatory condition.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: that is the first of the two available routes.
choice_analysis.D: Off-premises processing is permitted on either of the two conditions.
choice_analysis.E: Documentation does not supply the missing verification.

related_facts: The two routes are alternatives; either one satisfies the regulation
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates treat a careful check of the finished product as equivalent to verifying how it was made.

reasoning_steps: Identify that the processing occurred off the licensed premises
Test the facility against the Board-licensed route
Test the arrangement against the Massachusetts pharmacist verification route
